Interface GTNetResponseResult<T>

Type Parameters:
T - the type of the payload a successful answer carries
All Known Implementing Classes:
GTNetResponseResult.Deferred, GTNetResponseResult.Failed, GTNetResponseResult.Refused, GTNetResponseResult.Success
public sealed interface GTNetResponseResult<T> permits GTNetResponseResult.Success<T>, GTNetResponseResult.Refused<T>, GTNetResponseResult.Deferred<T>, GTNetResponseResult.Failed<T>
The outcome of a synchronous GTNet exchange, from the caller's point of view.

The HTTP status of a GTNet call is 200 for every protocol outcome, so "a body came back" says nothing about whether the peer served the request. A refusal such as GT_NET_LASTPRICE_MAX_LIMIT_EXCEEDED_S, a deferred acknowledgement and an error all arrive the same way as an answer, and a caller that only tests for a payload reads every one of them as "no data received" — which is indistinguishable from a peer that legitimately had nothing.

    GTNetResponseResult.Deferred<T>
    The peer took the request but has not decided; the answer arrives later as a message of its own.
    static final record 
    GTNetResponseResult.Failed<T>
    Nothing usable came back: no response, an unexpected code, or a payload that could not be read.
    static final record 
    GTNetResponseResult.Refused<T>
    The peer understood the request and declined to serve it — a limit, a missing grant, a cooling-off period.
    static final record 
    GTNetResponseResult.Success<T>
    The peer answered with one of the codes the caller declared it accepts.
